# @eduardoalvarez/arrecife

> GENERATED by `scripts/build-llms.mjs`. Do not edit by hand: the prose lives in
> `docs/llms.template.md` and the inventory comes out of the types on every
> build. `pnpm check:llms` fails if this file and the code stop saying the same
> thing.

The component library of Eduardo Álvarez's visual identity. React 19,
TypeScript, Tailwind v4, shadcn/ui on top of Radix.

This document is for an agent writing code in a project that consumes the
library. If you are working **inside** the Arrecife repo, the document is
`AGENTS.md`, not this one.

## First things first: do not reimplement what is already here

Before writing a card, a button, a header or a footer, look through the inventory
below. The library exists because five projects were each writing the same pieces
on their own and drifting apart. A new component hand-written in the consuming
project reintroduces exactly that problem.

Do not hand-write colors, sizes or spacing either. Every value in the system has
a token and a Tailwind utility; a `#hex` or a `p-[13px]` in the consuming project
is the sign that the wrong path was taken.

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @eduardoalvarez/arrecife
```

Requirements, and they are not optional:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| React | `^19.0.0` and `react-dom` `^19.0.0`, as peer dependencies |
| Tailwind | v4. **There is no v3 preset**: the output is `@theme`, which v3 does not understand |
| Node | `>=22.18.0` for the subpaths that run at build time (`./og`, `./tokens`) |

Radix, `clsx`, `tailwind-merge`, `class-variance-authority`, `date-fns` and
`react-day-picker` come as dependencies of the library. You do not need to
install or declare them.

**It ships no `lucide-react` and no icon library.** The glyphs the components
need are inline, inherit `currentColor` and measure 1em.

## Tailwind configuration

Two lines, in this order, in the project's entry stylesheet:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/tokens/theme.css";
```

Without the second one, the components mount with none of the system's styles:
the classes they use (`bg-surface-raised`, `text-h1`, `rounded-card`) do not
exist in a bare Tailwind.

Tailwind has to scan the library so it does not purge those classes. If the
project declares `@source`, include the package:

```css
@source "../node_modules/@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/dist";
```

### Light mode and dark mode

**Dark mode is primary and it is the default.** A dark project declares nothing.
A project in light mode declares the attribute on `<html>`:

```html
<html data-theme="light">
```

There is no `dark:` class. The variant available is `light:`, for the cases of
inverted light mode, and it is almost never needed: the tokens already switch on
their own.

### Fonts

The library declares the families **by name** and does not load them. The project
loads Bricolage Grotesque (`font-display`), Geist (`font-sans`) and JetBrains
Mono (`font-mono`) however it prefers — `next/font`, `@fontsource`, a `<link>`.
If it does not load them, the browser falls back and the typography looks wrong.

The name has to match **exactly** the one the tokens declare, and this has
already failed in two projects:

| Utility | Name the token asks for |
| --- | --- |
| `font-display` | `"Bricolage Grotesque"` |
| `font-sans` | `"Geist"` |
| `font-mono` | `"JetBrains Mono"` |

Several font packages publish them as `"Bricolage Grotesque Variable"` or
`"Geist Variable"`. Registering the `@font-face` under that name does NOT load
what the tokens ask for: the family falls back to the system silently, with no
console error. The `@font-face`'s `font-family` is an alias the project chooses,
so write it with the name from the table.

## What to import from where

The choice matters, for two different reasons. Four subpaths **do not drag React
in**, so they can be consumed from a worker, an `astro.config.mjs`, a build
script or a Satori generator. Another two ask for an **optional peer dependency**
that only whoever uses them installs.

| Subpath | Drags React | Also requires | What for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@eduardoalvarez/arrecife` | yes | — | Components, primitives, brand, `cn`. Re-exports tokens and theme |
| `@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/tokens` | **no** | — | The `tokens` object in JS. Satori, Astro, scripts |
| `@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/tokens/theme.css` | — | — | Tailwind v4's `@theme` |
| `@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/theme` | **no** | — | `themeScript` for the `<head>`, and reading or changing the mode |
| `@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/variants` | **no** | — | The class vocabulary: `buttonVariants`, `badgeVariants`, `CARD_SURFACE` |
| `@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/og` | **no** | — | The Open Graph templates for Satori |
| `@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/shiki` | **no** | — | The syntax highlighting theme |
| `@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/brand` | yes | — | Logo, isotype and mascot as components |
| `@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/form` | yes | `react-hook-form` | The form layer: labels, errors and `aria-*` |
| `@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/chart` | yes | `recharts` | The chart chassis and the series palette |
| `@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/assets/*` | — | — | The brand PNGs |

Importing the root from a build script to get one token is the mistake the
subpaths exist to prevent: it drags all of React into a worker that never mounts
it.

`./form` and `./chart` sit outside the root for the symmetric reason: if they
hung off the main index, the projects that draw no charts and use no React Hook
Form would have to install those dependencies anyway so their bundler could
resolve an import they never execute.

### Next, Server Components and `"use client"`

The root, `./brand`, `./form` and `./chart` ship `"use client"` in the published
`dist/`. They render React and their Radix primitives call `createContext` at
module scope, so without the directive a Next project with the App Router cannot
import them at all: it fails at build time with
`TypeError: (0 , r.createContext) is not a function`.

You do not add anything: importing `Button` from a Server Component works, and
the boundary is already where it belongs. What you should NOT do is wrap the
import in an adapter of your own marked `"use client"` — that was the workaround
before 0.6.0 and it pulled 272 KB of client chunk in for components that never
needed it.

The five portable subpaths do NOT carry the directive, and that is the half that
matters in a Server Component: `./tokens`, `./theme`, `./variants`, `./og` and
`./shiki` stay on the server. If all you need are classes — for a `<div>`, an
`<a>` or an Astro island you do not want to hydrate — import them from
`./variants` and nothing crosses to the client:

```tsx
// A Server Component, or an .astro frontmatter. No React reaches the browser.
import { buttonVariants, CARD_SURFACE } from '@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/variants';

<a className={buttonVariants({ variant: 'tertiary' })} href="/cursos">./ver_cursos →</a>
<div className={CARD_SURFACE}>…</div>
```

In Astro and in plain Vite the directive is inert — a string literal at the top
of a module. Rollup may warn `Module level directives cause errors when bundled`
and nothing else happens: one `dist` serves the Next projects and the Astro ones.

```ts
// Good, in an OG generator or in astro.config.mjs
import { tokens } from '@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/tokens';
import { arrecife } from '@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/shiki';

// Good, in the <head> of an Astro that mounts no React
import { themeScript } from '@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/theme';

// Bad: mounts React where it is not needed
import { tokens } from '@eduardoalvarez/arrecife';
```

### The theme, and the first-paint flash

`ThemeToggle` is the button; the hard part is in `./theme`. Without `themeScript`
inline in the `<head>`, the first paint comes out in the default mode and the
chosen one arrives a frame later: on a dark site the user left in light mode,
that is a white flash on every load.

```astro
---
import { themeScript } from '@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/theme';
---
<head>
  <!-- The site follows the reader's OS, falling back to dark. -->
  <script is:inline set:html={themeScript()} />

  <!-- Or: this site IS dark, and the OS is not consulted. -->
  <script is:inline set:html={themeScript({ base: 'dark' })} />
</head>
```

`base` is not «the fallback», it is «this site IS this mode». A stored choice
still wins over it, so the toggle keeps working — it sets what happens when
nobody has chosen yet. Use it when the project has already decided its mode and
does not want the OS overruling that.

It has to go INLINE. A `<script src>`, even a synchronous one, gets downloaded,
and the flash comes back. The script re-attaches on `astro:after-swap` because
view transitions replace the whole `<html>`.

### The social icons are namespaced

```tsx
// ❌ does not exist
import { GitHub } from '@eduardoalvarez/arrecife';

// ✅
import { social } from '@eduardoalvarez/arrecife';
<social.GitHub />
```

All nine: `GitHub`, `LinkedIn`, `X`, `Instagram`, `Discord`, `YouTube`, `Rss`,
`Email`, `Newsletter`. They live under a namespace because one of them is called
`X`, and loose it collides. `Newsletter` is the bell: a way to follow, like
`Rss`, named for what it means.

The internal glyphs — `Close`, `ChevronDown`, `Sun` — are **not exported** and
are not going to be: they are the primitives' minimum set. A component that needs
an icon receives it as a prop (`Stat` has `icon`, each `SocialLink` in `Footer`
has its own). Do not ask for them to be published: pass your own.

## Tokens

The source is a TypeScript object and the CSS output is generated from it, so the
same value is available in both places and they cannot disagree.

| Token | Custom property | Tailwind utility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `colors[mode].surfaceRaised` | `--color-surface-raised` | `bg-surface-raised` |
| `brand.hull` | `--color-brand-hull` | `bg-brand-hull` |
| `typeScale.h1` | `--text-h1` | `text-h1` (brings line-height, weight and tracking) |
| `fonts.display` | `--font-display` | `font-display` |
| `radius.card` | `--radius-card` | `rounded-card` |
| `spacing.stepLg` | `--spacing-step-lg` | `p-step-lg`, `gap-step-lg`, `mb-step-lg` |
| `spacing.section` | `--spacing-section` | `py-section`, `mb-section` |
| `control.md` | `--spacing-control-md` | `px-control-md` |
| `control.icon` | `--spacing-control-icon` | `size-control-icon` (42×42) |
| `gradient[mode].hero` | `--gradient-hero` | `gradient-hero` |
| `size.nav` | `--spacing-nav` | `h-nav` |
| `size.content` / `size.wide` | `--container-content` / `--container-wide` | `max-w-content` / `max-w-wide` |
| `limits.measure` | `--container-measure` | `max-w-measure` |
| `shadow.standard` | `--shadow-standard` | `shadow-standard` |
| `motion` | `--duration-standard`, `--ease-standard` | `duration-standard`, `ease-standard` |

`transition-standard` is the system's only transition and it can only animate
color and border: that is how the utility is written.

**The spacing steps carry `step` in the name and it is not optional.** `p-md` is
not an Arrecife class: in a Tailwind v4 project it lands on the numeric scale and
does nothing visible. Page rhythm is `p-step-md`, `gap-step-sm`, `py-step-xl`.
They carry a prefix because `xs, sm, md, lg, xl` are the names of Tailwind's
`--container-*` scale, and a `--spacing-md` of our own was swallowing `max-w-md`
across the whole project with nothing warning about it. `max-w-*`, `w-*` and
`h-*` belong to Tailwind and are used as they are. Migration guide from 0.2.0:
<https://github.com/Proskynete/arrecife/blob/main/docs/migration-0.3.md>.

## System rules the consuming code must not break

These are identity decisions, already measured. Breaking them produces code that
compiles and looks wrong, or that fails the project's accessibility audit.

1. **Zero literal hexes.** Every color comes from a token or its custom property.
2. **`Button variant="conversion"` appears once per screen.** It is not enforced
   at runtime; two on the same page are a design error.
3. **`Button variant="destructive"` is for the irreversible only.** Never for
   «cancel» on a form, and not inside an `AlertDialog` — there the confirm button
   stays `primary`, because the title, the focus on cancel and the no-click-outside
   already carry the weight. See `docs/decisions.md` § 21.
4. **`secondary` is never filled.** It is border and text.
5. **No entrance animations.** Modals, menus, tooltips and toasts appear where
   they will stay. The only exception is the `Button loading` spinner.
6. **Semantics and scale are independent.** An `h2` that has to look small is
   `<Text as="h2" variant="h3">`, never an `h3` that lies about the hierarchy.
7. **`textMuted` never goes over `surfaceRaised`**: it gives 4.07 in dark. Over a
   raised surface — menus, active tabs — the token is `textSecondary`.
8. **A background tinted with a semantic color carries text from a text token**,
   not from the semantic color. The color stays on the border and on the glyph.
   Putting `accent` over its own tint at 8 % gives 4.12 and does not reach AA.
9. **`Progress` requires `label`.** A bar with no accessible name does not say
   what it is about.
10. **`Button size="icon"` and `size="icon-sm"` require `aria-label`.** They carry
    no text. `icon` is 42×42 and is a page action; `icon-sm` is 32×32 and is for a
    dense table row.
11. **The mascot's faces only appear** in empty states, confirmations, errors,
    course progress and celebration. Never in a hero, pricing, services, contact
    or the CV.
12. **The fin is not a free parameter**: `foam` on a dark background, `color` on a
    light one. The components already choose it from the background.

## What the library does NOT do, on purpose

These are the confusions people run into most often when consuming it.

- **It does not ship Shiki.** It publishes the *theme*, not the highlighter.
  `CodeBlock` receives the code **already highlighted** by the project's tool.
- **It does not format dates.** `ArticleCard`, `TalkCard` and company receive the
  date already formatted by the project: the library imposes no locale.
  `dateTime` is separate, in ISO, for the `<time>` attribute.
- **`NewsletterForm` does not do the POST.** It is presentational: it takes
  `state` and emits `onSubmitEmail`. The call is made by the project with its own
  provider.
- **It ships no router.** The components with links accept `asChild` to wrap the
  framework's `Link`.
- **It ships no `data-testid`.** A composed part your test suite has to reach is
  reached with a slot: `ArticleCard`'s `tagAsChild`, `Breadcrumb`'s and
  `TableOfContents`'s `linkAsChild`. They hand you the element and its
  attributes and keep the classes. Do NOT select by structure or by a style
  class — a style class is not a contract and it changes when the style does.
- **It does not load fonts.** It declares them by name.
- **There is no Tailwind v3 preset.**

## Usage patterns

```tsx
import { Text, Button, Badge, cn } from '@eduardoalvarez/arrecife';
import type { TextProps } from '@eduardoalvarez/arrecife';

<Text variant="eyebrow" tone="muted">charlas</Text>
<Text as="h2" variant="h1">Escalar con criterio</Text>
<Text variant="body">Clamps itself to 68ch.</Text>
<Text variant="ui" measure={false}>No clamp, for a narrow cell.</Text>
```

`asChild` renders the child instead of the component's own element. It is how the
framework's link gets wrapped without losing the styles:

```tsx
<Button asChild>
  <Link href="/cursos">Ver los cursos</Link>
</Button>
```

`cn` is `clsx` + `tailwind-merge`. It is used to compose `className` without two
utilities from the same group fighting each other.

Open Graph, without React:

```ts
import satori from 'satori';
import { articleTemplate, OG } from '@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/og';

const svg = await satori(articleTemplate({ title, date, readingMinutes }), {
  width: OG.width,   // 1200
  height: OG.height, // 630
  fonts: [...],
});
```

Syntax highlighting, from the site's configuration:

```ts
import { arrecife } from '@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/shiki';

export default defineConfig({
  markdown: { syntaxHighlight: 'shiki', shikiConfig: { theme: arrecife } },
});
```

# Inventory

What follows comes out of the TypeScript compiler on every build. Only the props
**declared by the library** are listed: the ones inherited from an HTML element
or from a Radix primitive are summarised in the `Extends` line, and they are the
usual ones.

## Primitives

Imported from `@eduardoalvarez/arrecife`. 110 exports.

### Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, AccordionContent

Source: `src/primitives/accordion.tsx`

**Accordion**
The disclosure. Two projects asked for it: the portfolio FAQ and the course syllabus, which is literally a list of sections that open.

- Extends: `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof AccordionPrimitive.Root>`
- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**AccordionItem**
- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**AccordionTrigger**
The trigger IS the heading, so it goes INSIDE an `<h3>`: Radix wraps the button in `AccordionPrimitive.Header`, which renders whichever element you ask of it. Without that, a screen reader sees a list of loose buttons and loses the page structure, which is precisely what a FAQ needs to keep.

- Extends: `ComponentPropsWithoutRef< typeof AccordionPrimitive.Trigger >`

| prop | type | req. | default | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `headingLevel` | `4 \| 2 \| 3` |  | `3` | The level of the heading wrapping the trigger. |

**AccordionContent**
- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

### AlertDialogOverlay, AlertDialogContent, AlertDialogHeader, AlertDialogFooter, AlertDialogTitle, AlertDialogDescription, AlertDialogCancel, AlertDialogAction, AlertDialog, AlertDialogTrigger

Source: `src/primitives/alert-dialog.tsx`

**AlertDialogOverlay**
- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**AlertDialogContent**
No entrance animation, same as `Dialog`: it appears where it will stay.

- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**AlertDialogHeader**
- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**AlertDialogFooter**
Cancel to the LEFT of confirm on desktop and BELOW it on mobile, which is what `flex-col-reverse` gives: the DOM order puts cancel first — that is where focus goes — and in a column the thumb finds it where it should be without changing the tab order.

- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**AlertDialogTitle**
- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**AlertDialogDescription**
What is lost, spelled out. The `alertdialog` role makes this get announced up front, so «this action cannot be undone» does not go here on its own: what goes here is what gets deleted and what it takes down with it.

- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**AlertDialogCancel**
The one that takes focus on open.

- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**AlertDialogAction**
- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**AlertDialog**
The destructive confirmation. It is NOT a `Dialog` with different text, which is why it lives in its own file and on its own Radix primitive.

- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**AlertDialogTrigger**
- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

### Alert

Source: `src/primitives/alert.tsx`

- Extends: `Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'div'>, 'title'> & VariantProps<typeof alert>`

| prop | type | req. | default | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `emphasis` | `"subtle" \| "strong"` |  |  |  |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Replaces the variant's mono glyph. Never an emoji: if you need something else, it is an SVG from `glyphs`. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  |  |  |
| `variant` | `"accent" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "error"` |  |  |  |

### Avatar, AvatarImage, AvatarFallback, AvatarUpload

Source: `src/primitives/avatar.tsx`

**Avatar**
One for everything: the author's photo and anyone else's in the system. There is no separate `brand/Avatar` — a profile photo wearing the brand's skin is exactly this with a different `src`.

- Extends: `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof AvatarPrimitive.Root> & VariantProps<typeof avatar>`

| prop | type | req. | default | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` |  |  |  |

**AvatarImage**
- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**AvatarFallback**
Initials while the image loads, or when there is no image.

- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**AvatarUpload**
The avatar you can change. `Avatar` displays; this one also lets you pick.

- Extends: `Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'div'>, 'onSelect' \| 'children'> & VariantProps<typeof avatar>`

| prop | type | req. | default | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `accept` | `string` |  | `image/*` | What the system dialog accepts. |
| `disabled` | `boolean \| undefined` |  | `false` |  |
| `fallback` | `ReactNode` |  |  | Initials while there is no image. |
| `label` | `string` |  | `Cambiar la foto` | The control's accessible name. It is the only thing naming it: there is no visible text. |
| `onSelectFile` | `(file: File) => void` |  |  | Fires with the chosen file. The upload is the project's job. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` |  |  |  |
| `src` | `string` |  |  | The current image, already uploaded. The local preview beats it while it lasts. |

### Badge, CategoryBadge, MetricBadge

Source: `src/primitives/badge.tsx`

**Badge**
Three badge families, three components. Why there are three shapes and not one is in `variants/badge.ts`, next to the classes that make them.

- Extends: `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'span'> & VariantProps<typeof badge>`

| prop | type | req. | default | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"neutral" \| "accent" \| "warm" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "error"` |  |  |  |

**CategoryBadge**
- Extends: `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'span'>`

| prop | type | req. | default | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | `boolean \| undefined` |  | `false` | Selected filter: solid sand with ink on top. |

**MetricBadge**
- Extends: `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'span'>`

| prop | type | req. | default | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `boxed` | `boolean \| undefined` |  | `false` | Adds the hairline ring. By default a metric carries no box. |

### Button

Source: `src/primitives/button.tsx`

- Extends: `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'> & VariantProps<typeof button>`

| prop | type | req. | default | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `asChild` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Renders the child instead of a `<button>`, to wrap a link. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` |  |  | SVG glyph before the text. Hidden while loading. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Disables and announces `aria-busy`. Incompatible with `asChild`. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "icon" \| "icon-sm"` |  |  |  |
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "conversion" \| "secondary" \| "tertiary" \| "destructive" \| "destructiveOutline"` |  |  |  |

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

Source: `src/primitives/date-field.tsx`

A date field on the native control, not on a calendar of our own.

| `withTime` | `boolean \| undefined` |  | `false` | Adds the time to the field. It is the native `datetime-local`. |

### DialogOverlay, DialogContent, DialogHeader, DialogFooter, DialogTitle, DialogDescription, Dialog, DialogTrigger, DialogClose

**Dialog**
- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

### Progress

Source: `src/primitives/progress.tsx`

- Extends: `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof ProgressPrimitive.Root>`

| `tone` | `"accent" \| "warm"` |  | `accent` | Sand instead of biolume, for course progress. |

### Blockquote

Source: `src/components/blockquote/index.tsx`

The side bar is `accent`, the interactive color, because a quotation is somebody else's voice entering the text. It carries no decorative quote marks: the system's glyphs are SVG, and an ornamental quote adds nothing the border and the indent do not already say.

### CodeBlock

Source: `src/components/code-block/index.tsx`

`brand.hull` is «hull · outline and the background of code blocks», so a code block is dark in light mode too. That is why the root declares `data-theme="dark"`: everything inside — ink, hairline, accent — switches to the dark palette regardless of the page's theme. It is the system's only island of inverted theme, and it is deliberate.

- Extends: `Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'div'>, 'children'>`

| prop | type | req. | default | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | yes |  | The already-highlighted code, or flat text. |
| `copyText` | `string` |  |  | The text copied to the clipboard. Without it, the button is not shown. |
| `language` | `string` |  |  | The language label. Shown in the top bar. |

| `title` | `ReactNode` | yes |  |  |

## Forms

Imported from `@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/form` · requires `react-hook-form`. 7 exports.

### FormField, FormItem, FormLabel, FormControl, FormDescription, FormMessage, Form

Source: `src/form/index.tsx`

**FormField**
A controlled field. It wraps RHF's `Controller` and also publishes the name into context, which is where the label and the message read it from without having to repeat it three times.

- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**FormItem**
The field's box: label, control, help and message, in a column.

- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**FormLabel**
The label is NOT tinted red when the field fails.

- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**FormControl**
Wraps the control and wires its attributes: the `id` the label points at, the `aria-describedby` with the help and the message, and the `aria-invalid`.

- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**FormDescription**
The field's help text. It is always announced, error or not.

- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**FormMessage**
The validation message. With no error it renders nothing: a gap reserved for the failure shifts the rest of the form every time it appears.

- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**Form**
The layer that ties the controls to a form with validation and messages.

- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

## Charts

Imported from `@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/chart` · requires `recharts`. 5 exports.

### ChartContainer, ChartTooltip, ChartLegend, ChartTooltipContent, ChartLegendContent

Source: `src/chart/index.tsx`

**ChartContainer**
Wraps the chart in a `<figure>` with an accessible name and gives Recharts the concrete height it needs to measure itself.

- Extends: `Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'figure'>, 'title'>`

| prop | type | req. | default | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `height` | `number` |  | `320` | Height in pixels. Recharts needs a concrete one to measure itself. |
| `label` | `string` | yes |  | What the chart shows, in one sentence. Mandatory, like `Progress`'s `label`: a bar `<svg>` with no accessible name is not «a chart without a label», it is an empty region. |
| `summary` | `ReactNode` |  |  | What the chart says, in words. It goes in a visually hidden `figcaption`. |

**ChartTooltip**
Recharts' `Tooltip` with the system's defaults: no animation, and the cursor tinted `surfaceRaised`.

- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**ChartLegend**
- No own props: it passes through those of the element or primitive it wraps.

**ChartTooltipContent**
The tooltip's box. It is a system card — `surface`, control border, standard shadow — and not Recharts' white box, which in dark mode is a white rectangle on top of a dark panel.

- Extends: `{ active?: boolean \| undefined; payload?: readonly ChartPayloadItem[] \| undefined; label?: ReactNode; /** Formats the value. Without it, it is printed as is: the library imposes no locale. */ formatter?: ((value: unknown, item: ChartPayloadItem) => ReactNode) \| undefined; /** Hides the header, for a single-category chart. */ hideLabel?: boolean; className?: string; }`

| prop | type | req. | default | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | `boolean \| undefined` |  |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `formatter` | `(value: unknown, item: ChartPayloadItem) => ReactNode` |  |  | Formats the value. Without it, it is printed as is: the library imposes no locale. |
| `hideLabel` | `boolean` |  | `false` | Hides the header, for a single-category chart. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  |  |
| `payload` | `readonly ChartPayloadItem[]` |  |  |  |

**ChartLegendContent**
The legend, with the tooltip's same square swatch and the `label` scale.

- Extends: `{ payload?: readonly ChartPayloadItem[] \| undefined; className?: string; }`

| prop | type | req. | default | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |  |
| `payload` | `readonly ChartPayloadItem[]` |  |  |  |

## Exports that are not components

The root re-exports everything from `./tokens` and `./brand` for convenience.
Each one appears exactly once, under the most specific subpath that publishes
it: if the code does not mount React, that subpath is the one to import.

### `@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/tokens`

| export | type | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `brand` | `{ readonly body: "#3E7CB1"; readonly spots: "#C2D7E7"; readonly hull: "#0B1524"; }` | Brand — identical in both modes. |
| `colors` | `{ dark, light }` |  |
| `control` | `{ readonly sm: 14; readonly md: 22; readonly lg: 30; readonly icon: 42; readonly iconSm: 32; }` | Controls, from the document: `sm 8/14 · md 12/22 · lg 15/30 · icon 42×42`. |
| `dark` | `{ background, surface, surfaceRaised, border, hairline, hairlineHover, textPrimary, textSecondary, textMuted, accent, accentHover, accentOn, warm, warmHover, warmOn, success, warning, error, danger, dangerHover, dangerOn }` | Dark mode (primary). Contrast measured against `background` #091319. |
| `fonts` | `{ display, sans, mono }` |  |
| `gradient` | `{ dark, light }` |  |
| `light` | `{ background, surface, surfaceRaised, border, hairline, hairlineHover, textPrimary, textSecondary, textMuted, accent, accentHover, accentOn, warm, warmHover, warmOn, success, warning, error, danger, dangerHover, dangerOn }` | Light mode. Contrast measured against `background` #F6F2EA. `background` is WARM white: never #FFF as the page background. |
| `limits` | `{ readonly minScreenPx: 13; readonly minPrintPt: 12; readonly measure: "68ch"; }` | Hard legibility limits. |
| `motion` | `{ readonly duration: "150ms"; readonly easing: "ease-out"; readonly properties: "color, background-color, border-color, fill, stroke"; }` | 150ms ease-out — color and border only. The system animates neither position nor scale: states are communicated with border and color, not with movement. |
| `naming` | `{ readonly wordmark: "Eduardo Álvarez"; readonly mascot: "Tiburoncín"; readonly domain: "eduardoalvarez.dev"; }` | The wordmark always reads «Eduardo Álvarez». The mascot is called Tiburoncín and its name never appears inside the logo. |
| `radius` | `{ readonly chip: 6; readonly control: 10; readonly card: 14; readonly panel: 16; readonly pill: 999; }` |  |
| `series` | `{ readonly dark: readonly ["#35D6C0", "#F2A65A", "#3E7CB1", "#71919C"]; readonly light: readonly ["#0D7C6F", "#A65B27", "#3E7CB1", "#626A75"]; }` | The chart series palette. FOUR, for the same reason as the syntax palette: the system communicates with color and border, not with chromatic noise. |
| `shadow` | `{ readonly standard: "0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35)"; }` | A single level. There is no elevation scale. |
| `size` | `{ readonly nav: 64; readonly content: 760; readonly wide: 1180; }` |  |
| `spacing` | `{ readonly stepXs: 8; readonly stepSm: 12; readonly stepMd: 16; readonly stepLg: 26; readonly stepXl: 40; readonly section: 96; }` | Page rhythm. All five steps carry `step` in the name, and that is not decoration: it is the fix for a bug that never surfaced anywhere. |
| `syntax` | `{ background, identifier, literal, keyword, comment, invalid }` | The syntax highlighting palette. |
| `tagline` | `{ long, short, en }` |  |
| `tokens` | `{ colors, brand, fonts, typeScale, limits, radius, control, spacing, size, gradient, syntax, series, shadow, motion, tagline, naming }` | Every token in a single object, for Satori templates and generators. |
| `typeScale` | `{ display, stat, h1, h2, h3, body, lead, ui, label, tag, chip, meta, eyebrow }` |  |

### `@eduardoalvarez/arrecife/theme`

| export | type | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `applyTheme` | `(theme: Theme, persist?: boolean): void` | Sets the theme on `<html>` and persists it. |
| `currentTheme` | `(): Theme` | The theme currently in place, read from the DOM. |
| `preferredTheme` | `({ base }?: ThemeOptions): Theme` | The theme that applies: whatever was chosen, and with no choice, `base` if the site declared one, else whatever the system asks for. With no `prefers-color-scheme` declared, dark, which is primary. |
| `storedTheme` | `(): Theme \| null` | The stored preference, if any. `null` means «nobody has chosen», which is not the same as «chose dark»: with no choice, the system decides. |
| `THEME_ATTRIBUTE` | `"data-theme"` | The attribute the `[data-theme]` blocks in `theme.css` read. |
| `THEME_EVENT` | `"arrecife:theme"` | The event emitted when the theme changes. |
| `THEME_KEY` | `"arrecife-theme"` | The `localStorage` key. |
| `themeScript` | `({ base }?: ThemeOptions): string` | The script that goes INLINE in the `<head>`, before any stylesheet. |
| `toggleTheme` | `(): Theme` | Switches to the opposite one and returns whichever stuck. |
| `watchTheme` | `(onChange: (theme: Theme) => void, options?: ThemeOptions): () => void` | Subscribes to theme changes and returns the function that cancels it. |

Types (2): `Theme`, `ThemeOptions`.

# Where to look if this is not enough

- Storybook publishes every component with its stories and the props table
  generated from the types.
- The repo's `README.md`: the reasoning behind each decision, the contrast
  correction table and the release cycle.
- `docs/design-system.md` and `docs/brand-manual.md`: the identity documents,
  greppable.
- `docs/decisions.md`: the points where the code and the document did not say the
  same thing, each with its resolution.
- `AGENTS.md`: for working inside the library's repo.
